summary: Today’s pulse tracks Top Democrats raise corruption concerns after Trump involvement in Jensen Huang’s Nvidia reinstatement – live, Federal court clears way for army to detonate bomb-making material in Iowa, and Australian politics live: Taylor notes ‘tough year’ for Coalition party room; King Charles ‘deeply saddened’ by Meldrum’s death. Across Guardian, BBC, and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are jensen, nvidia, and trump. In the background, US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal and Butt of the joke: Trump impersonator mocks president at Canada press dinner keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Top Democrats raise corruption concerns after Trump involvement in Jensen Huang’s Nvidia reinstatement – live
headlines.description: Robert Garcia, top Democrat on House oversight, and Chris Van Hollen, vying for Senate leadership, join Republicans in expressing concern at return of CEO felled by affair scandal and Trump administration’s involvement Sign up to the Breaking News US email Nvidia ’s shares have surged by 31% at the start of trading following the news. The S+P 500 jumped 4.5% and is recovering nearly half of its brutal losses from last week, which was one of its worst since the 2008 financial crisis. Rallies for AI stocks had the Nasdaq composite up a market-leading 6.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,117 points. Here’s Trump ’s full social media post, in which he also called Jensen Huang “a Great Patriot and National Treasure”. The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World!

headlines.title: Federal court clears way for army to detonate bomb-making material in Iowa
headlines.description: Environmentalists sued last week to stop detonation of 68 barrels of lead azide over health and pollution concerns A federal appeals court cleared way for the US army to detonate several tons of degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant, hours after Donald Trump halted the planned demolition and urged the court to first sign off on what he called the safest way to resolve the situation. “I feel the proper course is to get rid of this longterm problem but, at the same time, have ordered the Military not to do so until such time as the Eighth Circuit agrees that we can go forward, and am further making this decision fully subject to the incoming Governor-Elect, Rob Sand, agreeing to the operation,” Trump said in a Truth Social post .

headlines.title: Australian politics live: Taylor notes ‘tough year’ for Coalition party room; King Charles ‘deeply saddened’ by Meldrum’s death
headlines.description: Unlike the federal budget, where we get plenty of notice of when it will be handed down, the government only gives us a few days notice for the mid-financial year economic and fiscal outlook (or Myefo). There’s still a fair bit of work to do to finalise it all, but we’ve made enough progress to be confident that at this stage there will be a modest net save in the budget. We’re not going to slash and burn in the budget where that would impact the payments that people receive or where it would impact some of the more sensitive parts of the economy. But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times. You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now. I think it’s a bit of a symbol of the quite extraordinary volatility, unpredictability that we’re seeing play out in markets in the AI sector, but more broadly as well.

headlines.description: Megaspeed has been accused of funneling AI chips to China after a former executive's affair with Jensen Huang became public.

headlines.title: Butt of the joke: Trump impersonator mocks president at Canada press dinner
headlines.description: Carney watches on as comedian lampoons US leader and his interest in men’s backsides at correspondents’ event Ottawa Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, was joined on stage in Ottawa by a Donald Trump impersonator who mocked the US president to raucous laughter from a crowd of politicians and journalists at a parliamentary press gallery dinner on Saturday. With coiffed hair and an ill-fitting suit, comedian Mark Critch – who portrays the president on the sketch show This Hour Has 22 Minutes – danced on to the stage and lampooned the trade war Trump started as well as the president’s threats to annex Canada.

headlines.description: California Congressman Rep. Jimmy Gomez says he will resign after a House Ethics report concluded Gomez's actions violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances."

headlinePool.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenes
headlinePool.description: Share price surges as chipmaker reverses decision to remove chief executive after US president ‘convinced’ its board Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment US politics – live updates Timeline: fall and comeback of Jensen Huang Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after Donald Trump directly intervened with the US AI chipmaker’s board of directors, in a stunning reversal of the tech billionaire’s downfall . Speaking on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s surprise announcement that Huang had been restored to the top job – less than two weeks after he resigned – Trump said that he had “convinced” the board to do it. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC. Huang had resigned after reports of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees.

headlinePool.title: Jimmy Gomez to resign after House ethics panel finds evidence of sexual misconduct
headlinePool.description: Democrat, who lost re-election bid, found to have made ‘unwelcome sexual advances’ towards House staffer Jimmy Gomez will resign from Congress after a House ethics report released on Monday found “substantial evidence” that the California Democrat had “engaged in sexual misconduct”, including by “making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer”. The 19-page report from the House ethics committee found that Gomez “made unwanted sexual advances” toward a House staffer on two occasions, “including an incident in which he made sexual contact with her and another in which he was ‘forceful’ with her in his congressional office”.

headlinePool.title: Republican senators criticize Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang
headlinePool.description: Outcry builds over Trump-backed move to bring back CEO as lawmakers call for Huang’s testimony before Congress US politics – live updates Republican lawmakers roundly criticized the Nvidia board’s decision to reinstate its chief executive, Jensen Huang, even after Donald Trump said he spoke “directly and indirectly” with board members and “convinced them” to bring him back. Pete Ricketts, a US senator from Nebraska, wrote on X that Huang’s “behavior does not support reinstatement”.

headlinePool.title: Iranian singer and four others receive lashes after performance without hijab
headlinePool.description: Western governments and rights groups have criticised flogging as torture and a violation of international law An Iranian singer and four members of her production team ⁠have each received 74 lashes after being sentenced for “offending public decency by producing and ⁠publishing obscene and ⁠immoral ​content online”, an Iranian news website said on Monday. Parastoo Ahmadi and the four ⁠others were also handed two-year bans on artistic and musical activities and travel, the Emtedad website ⁠quoted lawyer Mostafa Nili as saying.
